text_blocks.snippet: Vaccinated individuals can still experience COVID-19 symptoms, though they are generally less severe and shorter in duration compared to unvaccinated individuals. Common symptoms include fever, fatigue, sore throat, and a dry cough that may last for a few days. Loss of taste and smell can also occur, but may linger for a few weeks. In some cases, vaccinated individuals may experience more severe symptoms like productive coughs with chest pain, low oxygen levels, and require hospitalization, but these are less frequent.
